--- title: "Data quality" subtitle: "Session 7 · Topic 2.5 · Tue 15 Dec" format: revealjs --- ## Today ::: {.agenda} 1. What can be wrong with calculation data 2. Reading a messy export 3. Wrong types and mixed formats 4. Missing values 5. Duplicates 6. Units and physically impossible values 7. Failed calculations 8. A reusable cleaning function + checks ::: ## Garbage in, garbage out A surrogate model does not know that a value is wrong. It learns it. | Problem | Example | Effect on a model | |---|---|---| | wrong unit | load in kN in some rows | learns a fake relationship | | typo | thickness 196 mm instead of 19.6 | one point pulls the fit | | failed run | stress = 0 | "infinitely safe" designs | | duplicates | same run exported twice | over-weights some designs, leaks into the test set | | gaps | missing deflection | errors or silently dropped rows | # Reading a messy export {.divider} ## First attempt ::: {#611cfed6 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} raw = pd.read_csv("data/bracket_raw.csv") raw.head(3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
run_id;thickness_mm;fillet_radius_mm;load_N;E_GPa;max_stress_MPa;deflection_mm;safety_factor;solver_status
R205;8 2;4 6;553.0;192 8;262.4;1 756;1 353;converged
R160;17 2;5 5;1490.0;204 0;170.7;0 484;2 08;converged
R220;12 8;6 8;965.0;207 7;186.8;0 748;1 9;converged
``` ::: ::: One column only → the separator is not a comma. ## Second attempt ::: {#bdbdd43a .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} raw = pd.read_csv("data/bracket_raw.csv", sep=";", decimal=",") raw.head() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
run_id thickness_mm fillet_radius_mm load_N E_GPa max_stress_MPa deflection_mm safety_factor solver_status
0 R205 8.2 4.6 553.0 192.8 262.4 1.756 1.353 converged
1 R160 17.2 5.5 1490.0 204.0 170.7 0.484 2.080 converged
2 R220 12.8 6.8 965.0 207.7 186.8 0.748 1.900 converged
3 R175 10.0 2.9 213.0 207.1 76.6 NaN 4.634 converged
4 R185 17.3 1.3 2957.0 209.6 469.8 0.920 0.756 converged
``` ::: ::: ## What types did we get? ::: {#9896565e .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} raw.dtypes ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` run_id str thickness_mm float64 fillet_radius_mm float64 load_N str E_GPa float64 max_stress_MPa str deflection_mm float64 safety_factor float64 solver_status str dtype: object ``` ::: ::: - `load_N` and `max_stress_MPa` are **text**, although they should be numbers - why? Some values use a dot, some a comma; some say `n/a` ::: {#2c1e7141 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} raw["max_stress_MPa"].head(6).tolist() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ``` ['262.4', '170.7', '186.8', '76.6', '469.8', '300.5'] ``` ::: ::: ## Converting to numbers safely ::: {#7ca147aa .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} def to_number(col): """Text -> float; accepts decimal commas and dots, bad values become NaN.""" return pd.to_numeric(col.astype(str).str.replace(",", "."), errors="coerce") clean = raw.copy() for c in ["load_N", "max_stress_MPa"]: clean[c] = to_number(clean[c]) clean.dtypes[["load_N", "max_stress_MPa"]] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6} ``` load_N float64 max_stress_MPa float64 dtype: object ``` ::: ::: - `errors="coerce"` turns anything that is not a number into `NaN` (missing) - always work on a **copy** — keep the raw data untouched # Missing values {.divider} ## Finding them ::: {#e30f886b .cell execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code} clean.isna().sum() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=7} ``` run_id 0 thickness_mm 0 fillet_radius_mm 0 load_N 0 E_GPa 4 max_stress_MPa 3 deflection_mm 6 safety_factor 4 solver_status 0 dtype: int64 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#ecb8d339 .cell execution_count=8} ``` {.python .cell-code} clean[clean.isna().any(axis=1)].head() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=8} ```{=html}
run_id thickness_mm fillet_radius_mm load_N E_GPa max_stress_MPa deflection_mm safety_factor solver_status
3 R175 10.0 2.9 213.0 207.1 76.6 NaN 4.634 converged
25 R165 14.7 5.0 2773.0 196.4 436.7 NaN 0.813 converged
66 R086 9.1 7.9 1161.0 208.4 0.0 2.495 NaN diverged
132 R064 17.2 1.6 437.0 192.5 65.5 NaN 5.420 converged
152 R208 16.1 6.9 684.0 197.8 87.3 NaN 4.066 converged
``` ::: ::: ## What to do with missing values? | Option | When | pandas | |---|---|---| | drop the row | few rows, the value is essential (an output) | `dropna(subset=[...])` | | recompute | the value can be derived from others | e.g. SF = 355 / stress | | fill with a known value | a default really applies | `fillna(value)` | | fill with a statistic | only for inputs, only with care | `fillna(col.median())` | | re-run the calculation | best, if possible | — | ::: {.tip} Never fill a missing **output** (stress, deflection) with a mean: you invent a calculation result. For training data, re-run or drop. ::: ## In our data ::: {#5929de5f .cell execution_count=9} ``` {.python .cell-code} # E is missing in a few rows: material is the same steel, 200 GPa is a defensible nominal value clean["E_GPa"] = clean["E_GPa"].fillna(200.0) # deflection is an output: we cannot invent it before = len(clean) clean = clean.dropna(subset=["deflection_mm"]) print(f"dropped {before - len(clean)} runs without deflection") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` dropped 6 runs without deflection ``` ::: ::: ::: {.muted} Write down every decision like this. It goes into the model passport later. ::: # Duplicates {.divider} ## Exact duplicates and duplicated IDs ::: {#9860a6cd .cell execution_count=10} ``` {.python .cell-code} print(clean.duplicated().sum(), "identical rows") print(clean["run_id"].duplicated().sum(), "repeated run IDs") clean[clean["run_id"].duplicated(keep=False)].sort_values("run_id") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` 3 identical rows 3 repeated run IDs ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=10} ```{=html}
run_id thickness_mm fillet_radius_mm load_N E_GPa max_stress_MPa deflection_mm safety_factor solver_status
21 R006 19.7 4.2 2390.00 203.1 227.8 0.519 1.558 converged
83 R006 19.7 4.2 2390.00 203.1 227.8 0.519 1.558 converged
41 R078 15.9 4.1 1.59 198.0 223.0 0.675 1.592 converged
224 R078 15.9 4.1 1.59 198.0 223.0 0.675 1.592 converged
15 R151 17.9 1.3 929.00 203.4 138.6 0.269 2.561 converged
36 R151 17.9 1.3 929.00 203.4 138.6 0.269 2.561 converged
``` ::: ::: ::: {#2b9c1f17 .cell execution_count=11} ``` {.python .cell-code} clean = clean.drop_duplicates() assert clean["run_id"].is_unique ``` ::: ::: {.muted} Same ID but different values? That is not a duplicate — it is a conflict. Find out which one is right. ::: # Units and impossible values {.divider} ## Check ranges against physics and the plan ::: {#b51c2854 .cell execution_count=12} ``` {.python .cell-code} clean[["thickness_mm", "fillet_radius_mm", "load_N", "E_GPa"]].describe().loc[["min", "max"]] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=12} ```{=html}
thickness_mm fillet_radius_mm load_N E_GPa
min -13.4 1.0 0.51 190.0
max 196.0 8.0 2996.00 210.0
``` ::: ::: - negative thickness → sign error - thickness 190 mm → probably a missing decimal point (plan was 8–20 mm) - load around 1–3 → entered in **kN** instead of N (plan was 200–3000 N) ## Fixing what we understand ::: {#4a2e8dce .cell execution_count=13} ``` {.python .cell-code} in_kN = clean["load_N"] < 10 print(in_kN.sum(), "loads look like kN") clean.loc[in_kN, "load_N"] = clean.loc[in_kN, "load_N"] * 1000 bad_t = ~clean["thickness_mm"].between(8, 20) clean.loc[bad_t, ["run_id", "thickness_mm"]] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` 6 loads look like kN ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=13} ```{=html}
run_id thickness_mm
86 R107 -13.4
121 R032 196.0
``` ::: ::: ::: {#19b5e29c .cell execution_count=14} ``` {.python .cell-code} clean = clean[~bad_t] # unclear what the right value was -> remove and report print(len(clean), "runs left") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` 292 runs left ``` ::: ::: ::: {.muted} Fix only what you can explain (kN → N is certain). If you would have to guess: exclude and flag for re-calculation. ::: ## Outliers: suspicious, not automatically wrong ::: {#78521e06 .cell execution_count=15} ``` {.python .cell-code} q1, q3 = clean["max_stress_MPa"].quantile([0.25, 0.75]) iqr = q3 - q1 far = clean[clean["max_stress_MPa"] > q3 + 1.5 * iqr] # classic 1.5 × IQR rule print(len(far), "runs far above the rest") far[["run_id", "thickness_mm", "fillet_radius_mm", "load_N", "max_stress_MPa"]].head() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` 13 runs far above the rest ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=15} ```{=html}
run_id thickness_mm fillet_radius_mm load_N max_stress_MPa
10 R052 8.1 2.2 2708.0 1443.1
34 R258 9.3 4.4 2659.0 991.3
46 R290 9.2 1.2 2117.0 1026.2
47 R005 9.1 7.0 2897.0 1052.0
89 R292 8.6 4.1 2874.0 1252.8
``` ::: ::: - statistical rule (IQR) finds candidates; **physics** decides - thin plate + small radius + high load → high stress is real, keep it # Failed calculations {.divider} ## Solver status and zero results ::: {#2a47c828 .cell execution_count=16} ``` {.python .cell-code} clean["solver_status"].value_counts() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=16} ``` solver_status converged 288 diverged 4 Name: count, dtype: int64 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#20e7dbb7 .cell execution_count=17} ``` {.python .cell-code} clean[clean["solver_status"] != "converged"][["run_id", "max_stress_MPa", "safety_factor"]] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=17} ```{=html}
run_id max_stress_MPa safety_factor
66 R086 0.0 NaN
181 R098 0.0 NaN
202 R213 0.0 NaN
253 R232 0.0 NaN
``` ::: ::: ::: {#18a8dc38 .cell execution_count=18} ``` {.python .cell-code} clean = clean[clean["solver_status"] == "converged"] clean = clean.dropna(subset=["max_stress_MPa"]) print(len(clean), "runs left") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` 285 runs left ``` ::: ::: ## Consistency checks between columns ::: {#1a9af2f4 .cell execution_count=19} ``` {.python .cell-code} recomputed = 355 / clean["max_stress_MPa"] diff = (recomputed - clean["safety_factor"]).abs() print("max difference:", round(diff.max(), 4)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` max difference: 0.0005 ``` ::: ::: - derived columns must agree with their sources - physics: deflection should grow with load and fall with thickness — check later in EDA # Making it repeatable {.divider} ## One cleaning function ::: {#cb9d8478 .cell execution_count=20} ``` {.python .cell-code} def clean_bracket(path): """Read and clean a raw bracket export. Returns (clean DataFrame, report dict).""" df = pd.read_csv(path, sep=";", decimal=",") report = {"rows_in": len(df)} for c in ["load_N", "max_stress_MPa"]: df[c] = to_number(df[c]) df = df.drop_duplicates() df.loc[df["load_N"] < 10, "load_N"] *= 1000 # kN -> N df["E_GPa"] = df["E_GPa"].fillna(200.0) df = df[df["solver_status"] == "converged"] df = df[df["thickness_mm"].between(8, 20)] df = df.dropna(subset=["max_stress_MPa", "deflection_mm"]) df["safety_factor"] = 355 / df["max_stress_MPa"] # recompute, consistent report["rows_out"] = len(df) return df.reset_index(drop=True), report data, rep = clean_bracket("data/bracket_raw.csv") rep ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=20} ``` {'rows_in': 303, 'rows_out': 285} ``` ::: ::: ## Checks that stop bad data ::: {#495c7e84 .cell execution_count=21} ``` {.python .cell-code} def validate(df): assert df["run_id"].is_unique, "duplicate run IDs" assert df.notna().all().all(), "missing values left" assert df["thickness_mm"].between(8, 20).all(), "thickness out of plan range" assert df["load_N"].between(200, 3000).all(), "load out of plan range (unit?)" assert (df["max_stress_MPa"] > 0).all(), "non-positive stress" return True validate(data) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=21} ``` True ``` ::: ::: ::: {.tip} Put `clean_bracket` and `validate` in a `.py` file and commit them. New export from the solver → one line to get clean, checked data. ::: ## Your turn (25 min) ::: {.exercise} Start from `bracket_raw.csv` yourself (do not copy the slides): 1. Read it correctly and list every problem you find (types, gaps, duplicates, ranges, status). 2. For each problem, decide: fix, drop, or flag — and write why in a comment. 3. Write `clean_bracket(path)` returning the clean data and a report of how many rows were removed **for which reason**. 4. Compare your clean data with `bracket.csv` (the reference): same number of rows? Same mean stress? ::: ## Summary - read with the right `sep` and `decimal`; check `dtypes` first - `pd.to_numeric(..., errors="coerce")` for mixed text/number columns - missing values: never invent outputs; document what you filled and why - duplicates: `duplicated`, `drop_duplicates`, unique IDs - ranges: compare with the plan and with physics; fix only what you can explain - one cleaning function + `assert` checks = repeatable **Next session:** reshaping and aggregation — `groupby`, pivot tables, merging tables. ## Practice at home (~1 h) - finish your `clean_bracket` with a reason-by-reason report; commit it - if you have an export from your own solver: write a first cleaning function for it
